lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.45 - A Listen and number

details: Listen and number checks understanding of numbers by linking what students hear to the correct images. Numbering reinforces sound–image association and strengthens recognition of key vocabulary.
Look for careful listening and accurate numbering of each image.
“Let’s take a big family trip to the zoo! What animals can you see? And what jobs do your family members have?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.45 - B. Listen and choose

details: Listen and choose develops listening comprehension skills by having students compare what they hear with three different images.
Look for careful listening, correct responses based on the audiotrack and good comprehension.
“Can you hear our friends’ conversations? What animals are they looking at? Who are they talking about?”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.99 - A Look and match

details: Look and match checks understanding of key vocabulary by linking each sentence to the correct picture. Matching reinforces meaning and supports early reading comprehension.
Look for correct matching of each sentence to the correct image, accurate recognition of target vocabulary and students using picture clues to support understanding.
“I’ve made some sketches of some of the animals and people we’ve seen, but I forgot to write down what each one is of. Can you help me label them?”

Look for correct sentence completion based on the images shown, accurate use of vocabulary and neat handwriting.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.46 - C. Listen and read

details: Listen and read develops key listening and reading comprehension by helping students follow the story while hearing the correct pronunciation. Reading allows students to practise their pronunciation.
Look for careful listening, eyes on the text and accurate tracking of the words.
“My friend has sent us some of his pictures from the zoo, too!”
